transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Meeting: Dry run: Webinar - Running LLM inference for regulated workloads (FinServ + Healthcare)
Date: 2026-02-10
Time: 09:00 - 09:52 PT
Duration: 52 min
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai

Attendees:
- Noura El-Khoury (Redwood, Events)
- Camila Reyes (Redwood, VP Marketing)
- Soojin Lee (Redwood, Product Marketing)
- Ethan Wallace (Redwood, Content)
- Ben Carter (Redwood, Growth)
- Markus Klein (Redwood, Solutions Engineering)
- Fatima Noor (Redwood, Solutions Engineering)
- Dr. Aisha Rahman (Redwood, CISO)
- Olga Petrov (Redwood, GRC)
- Tyler Benson (Redwood, Marketing Ops)

---

[00:00] Noura El-Khoury: Alright, cool, I think we’re recording. This is the dry run for Thursday’s regulated workloads webinar. Goal is run-of-show, timing, and then we’ll do like a quick Q and A gauntlet.

[00:14] Camila Reyes: Yep. And we should be pretty picky on wording. We’re gonna have security folks listening for, you know, any over-claims.

[00:23] Soojin Lee: I’ll drive the deck first, then hand to Markus for the demo, then Aisha for the “security posture and boundaries” slide, then back to me for CTA. That’s the plan.

[00:36] Noura El-Khoury: Perfect. Tyler, can you just confirm chat/Q&A logistics? Like, who’s moderating.

[00:41] Tyler Benson: Yeah. I’ll monitor Q&A queue in the webinar tool. Ethan can watch chat for like “can you repeat the link” type questions. We’ll have the landing page URL pinned.

[00:54] Ethan Wallace: Yep.

[00:56] Noura El-Khoury: Great. Soojin, go ahead.

---

[01:00] Soojin Lee: Okay, slide one. Title: “Running LLM inference for regulated workloads: latency, cost, and auditability.” I’ll do a 45-second intro: we’re seeing teams stuck between hosted APIs that are fast to start but don’t pass security review, and self-host that passes security but becomes an ops tax.

[01:21] Camila Reyes: Can we avoid saying “don’t pass security review” like universally? Maybe “can stall in security review” or “raise questions.”

[01:28] Soojin Lee: Yeah, fair. “Can stall in security review.”

[01:32] Soojin Lee: Slide two is the agenda. I’ll keep it tight: (1) common regulated LLM use cases, (2) deployment model decision points hosted/dedicated/private, (3) reference architecture, (4) demo, (5) Q&A.

[01:48] Noura El-Khoury: Timing check: we want 30 min content, 10 min Q&A, 5 min buffer.

[01:55] Soojin Lee: Yep.

[01:56] Soojin Lee: Slide three: “What we mean by regulated.” I list FinServ: comms review, agent assist, KYC document extraction, and Healthcare: clinical summarization, patient messaging classification, coding support. And I’ll say: regulated means you need predictable controls—data handling, residency, retention, audit trails.

[02:19] Dr. Aisha Rahman: On “clinical summarization,” we should say “where permitted by policy,” because PHI may be involved. Just keep it as “PHI-sensitive workflows.”

[02:28] Soojin Lee: Got it.

[02:30] Soojin Lee: Slide four: the thesis. “Model choice is commoditizing; serving is the differentiator.” And the wedge for us is “Hosted → Dedicated → Private” with a consistent API.

[02:44] Ben Carter: Quick note: the slide copy says “start hosted, migrate to VPC in days.” That feels too strong.

[02:50] Soojin Lee: Yeah, that was from an earlier draft. We can soften to “in a predictable, staged path.”

[02:56] Camila Reyes: Yeah, say “reduce time-to-approval” not “in days.”

[03:01] Soojin Lee: Okay.

[03:03] Soojin Lee: Slide five: deployment decision tree. Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private in VPC or on-prem. The point: you can keep the same SDK and move boundaries. I’ll call out the typical triggers: data sensitivity, tenant isolation, audit logging requirements, and network restrictions.

[03:22] Markus Klein: And mention performance triggers too. Like, dedicated gives you consistent throughput, less noisy neighbor.

[03:27] Soojin Lee: Yeah. “Predictable throughput and tail latency.”

[03:31] Soojin Lee: Slide six: “Security and compliance: what questions show up first.” This is where we need to be careful. I currently have bullets: encryption in transit/at rest, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration options), SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs export, retention controls, data residency.

[03:53] Olga Petrov: On the slide it says “SOC2 certified.” We should not say “certified.” Say “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA” or “SOC 2 Type II audited.”

[04:03] Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1. And avoid implying HIPAA certification. We can say we support HIPAA-aligned controls and can sign BAAs depending on the engagement, but that’s legal.

[04:13] Ethan Wallace: So we should literally add a Q&A answer that is like “we can discuss BAA/DPA during security review; talk to your AE.”

[04:19] Camila Reyes: Yes.

[04:21] Soojin Lee: Okay, I’ll update slide language.

[04:24] Soojin Lee: Slide seven is “Reference architecture: Private in customer VPC.” I show request flow from customer app → private endpoint → Redwood control plane (or private control plane? depends) → inference runtime in customer boundary, plus logging pipeline to SIEM.

[04:42] Fatima Noor: Quick correction: in the diagram we should label it “customer-managed networking” and “Redwood-managed runtime components” depending on the mode. People will ask “who owns what.”

[04:52] Dr. Aisha Rahman: And for logging, be explicit: audit logs about admin actions and API access are available; app logs are customer-owned. We don’t want it to sound like we’re mirroring all prompts.

[05:06] Soojin Lee: Yep.

[05:08] Soojin Lee: Slide eight: “Operational model.” This is the Redwood vs customer responsibility split. I’m going to say: Redwood supports install/upgrade path, monitoring hooks, and guidance; customer controls VPC policies, key management, and SIEM integration.

[05:26] Markus Klein: Nice.

[05:27] Soojin Lee: Then I hand to Markus for demo.

[05:32] Noura El-Khoury: Before demo, can we time check? Where are we.

[05:35] Soojin Lee: If I actually talk, that’s about 8 minutes.

[05:39] Noura El-Khoury: Good.

---

[05:42] Markus Klein: Alright, I’ll share screen. For the live webinar, I’m doing a pre-recorded backup, but primary is live demo. The flow: show Console: per-route latency, token cost breakdown, then show a rollout policy with fallback, and finish with audit log export settings.

[06:01] Ben Carter: Do we have the audit logs UI in the Console demo tenant? Last time it was like hidden behind a feature flag.

[06:07] Markus Klein: Good catch. I need to confirm. If it’s not stable, I’ll show a screenshot slide instead.

[06:13] Tyler Benson: I can check with product flag config after this.

[06:17] Markus Klein: Okay. So demo script:
- 0:00 to 1:30: “Here’s the dashboard, here’s p95 latency, here’s throughput.”
- 1:30 to 3:30: “Cost view: tokens in/out, batching, cache hit rate.”
- 3:30 to 6:00: “Rollout: canary, A/B, and fallback policy.”
- 6:00 to 7:30: “Security: SSO/RBAC, audit log export, key integration notes.”

[06:41] Camila Reyes: That’s 7:30. Please don’t go over.

[06:44] Markus Klein: Yeah, I’ll set a timer.

[06:46] Markus Klein: Also, I’m going to say “we can integrate with your KMS.” But I want to be careful, like, it’s not every KMS on the planet.

[06:55] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Say “supports integration with major cloud KMS offerings; specifics depend on deployment mode.” That’s safer.

[07:03] Olga Petrov: And if someone asks HSM, we say “options available, we’ll confirm based on your requirements,” and route to security review.

[07:10] Markus Klein: Yep.

[07:12] Fatima Noor: Also for Private, people ask “is it fully air-gapped.” We should have a consistent answer: “We can support on-prem and restricted environments; exact architecture and update mechanism depends on the package.” Don’t say “fully airgapped” unless we’re 100%.

[07:27] Camila Reyes: Good.

[07:29] Markus Klein: Let me do a 60-second snippet like I would on the webinar.

[07:33] Markus Klein: “So what you’re looking at here is the Redwood Console. For regulated teams, the main issue is not just average latency, it’s tail latency and predictability. Here’s p95, broken down by model route. Here’s token cost. If you enable workload-aware batching, you’ll see unit cost come down, but we keep your SLO by bounding batch delay. And then on rollouts, you can canary a new model version and set a fallback route if error rate or latency spikes.”

[08:06] Ethan Wallace: Small thing: you said “bounded batch delay.” That’s good, but maybe define it in one clause.

[08:11] Markus Klein: Yeah, “we cap how long a request waits to be batched.”

[08:15] Camila Reyes: And don’t say “guarantee” anywhere.

[08:18] Markus Klein: Right.

[08:20] Noura El-Khoury: Great. Aisha, you’re up after Markus to anchor security posture.

---

[08:25] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Cool. My section is like two minutes max. I’m going to say: “We expect security review early. Here’s how to think about boundaries.” Then I list: identity controls (SSO/SAML, RBAC), encryption in transit, key management integration options, audit logging and export, retention/residency configuration by deployment mode.

[08:49] Dr. Aisha Rahman: And I’ll say: “We can share our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA.” That’s the line.

[08:55] Olga Petrov: Also add: “We have a standard security packet and questionnaire responses.” That helps.

[09:00] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yep.

[09:02] Camila Reyes: Also: a lot of prospects will ask “Do you store prompts and outputs.” We need the crisp answer.

[09:09] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Right. The crisp safe answer is: “Data handling depends on deployment mode and configured retention. In Private deployments, data stays within your environment boundaries as designed. For hosted, we minimize data retention and can discuss configuration options; we can share specifics in the security FAQ.” We don’t want to get into a long rabbit hole on the webinar.

[09:30] Soojin Lee: I’ll also say “we’ll follow up with the security FAQ doc.”

---

[09:34] Soojin Lee: For CTA slide, I’m planning: “If you’re evaluating regulated workloads, schedule a 30-minute security + architecture review. We’ll map your deployment constraints and share the reference architecture and FAQ.”

[09:49] Ben Carter: We should put the exact link and the alternative CTA, like “request the deck.” Some people aren’t ready to talk.

[09:55] Camila Reyes: Yes, but primary CTA should be meeting. Secondary is “get the checklist.”

[10:01] Ethan Wallace: I can create a one-pager “regulated inference checklist” as follow-up. But maybe not for Thursday.

[10:06] Camila Reyes: Not for Thursday.

[10:08] Noura El-Khoury: Ok. Now Q&A rehearsal. Tyler, can you throw questions.

---

[10:14] Tyler Benson: Alright, question one, classic: “Are you HIPAA compliant?”

[10:19] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Answer: “We support HIPAA-aligned security controls and can discuss signing a BAA as part of an enterprise engagement. The right next step is a security review where we can share details under NDA.”

[10:32] Olga Petrov: Add: “We’ll align with your policies and required administrative safeguards.” Keep it general.

[10:38] Soojin Lee: Got it.

[10:40] Tyler Benson: Question two: “Do you store prompts, responses, or embeddings?”

[10:45] Dr. Aisha Rahman: “In Private deployments, data stays within the customer environment boundary as designed, and you control retention. In hosted, retention and logging are configured to support operations and security; we can share current defaults and options in our security FAQ and during security review.”

[11:04] Camila Reyes: That’s good, but I’d like one sentence on “we don’t use your data to train models.”

[11:10] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes. “We do not use customer prompts or outputs to train our models.”

[11:16] Ethan Wallace: I’ll add that to the canned answers.

[11:19] Tyler Benson: Question three: “Can you do data residency in EU only?”

[11:23] Fatima Noor: “We support region selection in supported cloud regions; for strict residency requirements, Dedicated or Private is typically the right fit. We’ll validate which regions match your needs.”

[11:36] Soojin Lee: And avoid listing exact regions live unless we’re sure.

[11:39] Fatima Noor: Exactly.

[11:41] Tyler Benson: Question four: “Is Private the same as on-prem?”

[11:46] Markus Klein: “Private is the deployment model where you run Redwood in your environment boundary—commonly a customer VPC, and in some cases on-prem. The goal is consistent API plus operational tooling across modes.”

[11:58] Dr. Aisha Rahman: And say “networking is customer-managed.”

[12:02] Markus Klein: Yep.

[12:04] Tyler Benson: Question five: “Do you support customer-managed encryption keys with HSM?”

[12:10] Dr. Aisha Rahman: “We support integration with major KMS providers and can discuss HSM-based key management options based on your deployment requirements. We’ll confirm specifics during the security review.”

[12:23] Camila Reyes: Great.

[12:25] Tyler Benson: Question six: “How do you compare to Bedrock / Azure OpenAI?”

[12:31] Soojin Lee: “Those are solid options, especially if you’re already standardized on a hyperscaler. Where Redwood is different is performance and operational control for inference—predictable latency and cost, and a unified path to Dedicated and Private with consistent tooling, plus rollouts and fallback that are built for production.”

[12:52] Markus Klein: And if pushed: “we can bring your own open models,” versus being limited to one provider’s catalog.

[12:58] Soojin Lee: Yep.

[13:00] Camila Reyes: But careful not to say “we’re always cheaper.” Say “we help you measure and optimize.”

[13:05] Soojin Lee: Right.

---

[13:08] Noura El-Khoury: Okay, let’s jump to run-of-show and timing. We just did content in ~13 minutes, which is good for the dry run, but live will be more like 25.

[13:19] Noura El-Khoury: I want to tighten speaker handoffs. Soojin: “And now Markus will show…” Markus: “What you just saw…” Aisha: “Here’s what security teams ask…” Then back to Soojin for CTA.

[13:33] Markus Klein: I’ll add the “what you just saw” recap. It’s a good point.

[13:37] Ethan Wallace: For the moderator, we should have a line to buy time if there’s silence. Like, “Drop your questions in Q&A. We’ll also cover common ones.”

[13:46] Noura El-Khoury: I can do that.

[13:49] Ben Carter: On the landing page, do we say “Private in your VPC” or “Private control plane”? The copy is currently “Private control plane.”

[13:57] Soojin Lee: We should say “Private deployment in your VPC” and then optional “private control plane” as a deeper detail. The webinar audience might not care about control plane semantics.

[14:08] Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1. Avoid confusing terms. People hear “control plane” and assume we’re in their network.

[14:15] Fatima Noor: Also: for the architecture slide, we should show “customer SIEM” arrow and label it “export” not “stream all data.”

[14:24] Soojin Lee: I’ll update.

---

[14:27] Camila Reyes: One more messaging landmine: “zero retention.” We are not saying that. We can say “configurable retention” and “minimize retention where possible.”

[14:37] Soojin Lee: Yep. I’ll scrub that phrase across the deck.

[14:41] Olga Petrov: And for audit logs, say “audit logging available; retention/export options are available depending on deployment mode.” Not “seven years.” We got asked that on MedOrbit.

[14:52] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yep. If they want “seven years,” we say “we can export to your system of record.”

[14:59] Markus Klein: That’s a good answer.

[15:02] Ethan Wallace: I’ll craft that as: “We export audit logs to your SIEM / storage for long-term retention according to your policy.”

---

[15:09] Tyler Benson: Quick ops note: we’re capturing registrant UTMs and pushing to HubSpot. For high-intent leads (enterprise domains + viewed landing page + attended >20 min) we’ll Slack #sales and #solutions-eng.

[15:23] Camila Reyes: Great.

[15:25] Noura El-Khoury: Can we do a final quick run from Soojin opening to end of Aisha section, but like speed-run with the actual handoff phrases? 5 minutes.

[15:33] Soojin Lee: Sure.

[15:35] Soojin Lee: “Welcome everyone, today we’re talking about running LLM inference for regulated workloads. If you’re in FinServ or Healthcare, you’re probably balancing performance with auditability and deployment constraints… We’ll cover common use cases, how to think about hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments, and show you what this looks like in the Redwood Console.”

[15:56] Soojin Lee: “At a high level, our view is that model choice is expanding fast, but the hard part is serving in production: predictable latency, cost, and reliability, in the deployment model that passes your security review.”

[16:11] Soojin Lee: “Here’s the decision tree: hosted for speed, dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation, private for VPC or on-prem boundaries. Same API, same operational tooling.”

[16:23] Soojin Lee: “Now I’m going to hand it to Markus to show what this looks like in practice.”

[16:28] Markus Klein: “Thanks Soojin. I’ll keep this to about seven minutes. First, in the Console you can see tail latency and throughput by route. Next, unit economics: token in/out, and how batching and caching changes your cost without blowing up SLOs. And lastly, production controls like canary rollouts and fallback, plus how you can route audit logs into your systems.”

[16:52] Markus Klein: “What you just saw is the operational layer teams need when they’re moving from prototype to regulated production.”

[16:58] Markus Klein: “Aisha will now cover the security posture and how we handle the common questions we hear from CISOs and GRC.”

[17:05] Dr. Aisha Rahman: “Thanks Markus. In regulated environments, security review happens early. The key is clarity on boundaries: identity and access controls, encryption, key management integration, audit logging and export, and retention/residency configuration by deployment mode. We can share our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, and we have a standard security packet to accelerate reviews.”

[17:28] Dr. Aisha Rahman: “If you have strict data sensitivity requirements, Private deployments are typically where teams land, because you can keep data within your environment boundary and align retention with your policies.”

[17:40] Camila Reyes: That was solid. Just be careful with “keep data within your boundary” — it’s true, but don’t imply “no metadata” or something. Maybe “keep inference traffic and data within your boundary as designed.”

[17:52] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yeah, fair, I’ll add “as designed.”

[17:56] Noura El-Khoury: Perfect. That’s the core.

---

[18:00] Noura El-Khoury: Final checklist: Soojin scrubs deck for “certified,” “zero retention,” and “in days.” Markus confirms the audit log demo UI availability, otherwise screenshot. Tyler confirms form routing + UTM capture. Ethan drafts canned Q&A. Security/GRC gives webinar-safe phrasing.

[18:18] Ben Carter: Also SEO metadata on the landing page is already set for “regulated inference” keywords. We’ll add partner logo after approvals.

[18:26] Camila Reyes: Partner logo must be approved. Don’t add last minute.

[18:30] Noura El-Khoury: Yep.

[18:32] Ethan Wallace: Who is actually answering questions live? Like, are we doing “Aisha takes security, Markus takes technical”?

[18:39] Noura El-Khoury: That’s the plan. I’ll moderate. If there’s procurement/legal, we’ll say “we’ll follow up” and route to sales.

[18:48] Camila Reyes: And keep answers short. We want meetings.

[18:52] Markus Klein: lol. Understood.

[18:54] Dr. Aisha Rahman: I’ll also say: “We can go deeper in a security review.” That’s the bridge.

[19:00] Noura El-Khoury: Cool. We’re done early. Any last concerns?

[19:04] Olga Petrov: Just please don’t mention specific retention periods or claim “immutable logs” unless we specify it’s via customer storage/WORM. People hear that and then it becomes a contractual item.

[19:15] Soojin Lee: Noted.

[19:17] Camila Reyes: Great. Thanks all.

[19:20] Noura El-Khoury: Ending recording. Thanks.
